chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The general public claim that the allegiance of Abu Bakr, when the people gathered, was with the Pleasure of Allah, glorified is His mention, and Allah would not afflict the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after him.'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do they not recite the Book of Allah? Is it not that Allah says: And Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him; so if he dies or is killed, will you turn back upon your heels? And whoever turns back upon his heels, he will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful.'

He said: I said to him, 'They interpret it in another way.' So he said: 'Has not Allah, Exalted and Glorified, informed about those before them from the nations that they differed after the clear proofs came to them?'

Where He said: And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, the clear proofs, and supported him with the Holy Spirit. And if Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them, but they differed; so there were some of them who believed and some who disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have fought one another, but Allah does what He intends.
And in this is evidence that the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) differed after him, so there were some of them who believed and some who disbelieved.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq use the Quran to explain the differences among the companions after the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the Sunni claim that the allegiance to Abu Bakr was a unified act of divine pleasure by citing Quranic verses that predict post-prophetic division. He draws a parallel between the companions' differing beliefs and the strife among previous nations, such as the followers of Jesus, who divided into believers and disbelievers despite receiving clear proofs. This highlights the Shia view that the community's split was a natural consequence of human free will and divine decree, rather than a singular, error-free consensus.

en.hubeali: H 14846 – Ibn Mahboub, from Amro Bin Abu Al-Maqdaam, from his father who said:

I said to Abu Ja’farasws that: ‘The generality (of the Muslims) are alleging that the pledging of the allegiances to Abu Bakr where the people gathered was with the Pleasure of Allahazwj and Allahazwj did not like the strife (Fitna) in the community of Muhammadsaww after himsaww.

So Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Have you not recited the Book of Allahazwj? Has not Allahazwj said: “[3:144] And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; the messengers have already passed away before him; if then he dies or is killed will you turn back upon your heels? And whoever turns back upon his heels, he will by no means do harm to Allah in the least and Allah will reward the grateful”

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘They are explaining it upon another perspective’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Has not Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Informed about those who were before them from the communities who had differed from after the Proofs had come to them,

where Heazwj Said: “[2:253] and We gave clear miracles to Isa son of Marium, and strengthened him with the holy spirit. And if Allah had pleased, those after them would not have fought one with another after clear arguments had come to them, but they disagreed; so there were some of them who believed and others who denied; and if Allah had pleased they would not have fought one with another, but Allah brings about what He intends”
, and in this is the evidence against the companions of Muhammadsaww who had differed among (themselves) after himsaww. “So there were some of them who believed and others who denied”.
